result.title: EVEWorld: Physical Evolution Supervision for Embodied World Models
result.summary: Embodied world models enable scalable simulation of embodied interactions for robot learning. However, existing models are prone to Model Laziness, as they focus on visual fidelity at the expense of physical reasoning and lack process-level supervision over the temporal dynamics of manipulated objects. In this work, we propose EVEWorld, a physical evolution-supervision framework for physically consistent target evolution. EVEWorld consists of two components: Instance-Guided Restoration (IGR) and Temporal Instance Alignment (TIA). First, IGR promotes instance consistency through restoration supervision. Second, TIA promotes cross-frame consistency by aligning target instances across adjacent frames. We further introduce the Model Laziness Rate (MLR), a metric that measures persistent violations of instance consistency in generated trajectories. Extensive experiments on DreamGenBench, EWMBench, and PBench demonstrate the effectiveness of EVEWorld, notably achieving an 87.5% reduction in MLR compared with GigaWorld-0. On the WorldArena 2.0 Track 1 leaderboard, our model ranks 6th in JEPA Similarity and 17th overall, which further validates the performance of our evolution supervision strategy.

AI.brief_summary: EVEWorld 面向具身世界模型，提出实例引导复原与跨帧实例对齐两种监督，以缓解生成轨迹中忽略物理演化的「模型惰性」，并给出 Model Laziness Rate 指标衡量实例一致性违规。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「过程级监督跨帧目标实例演化」的思路可能与 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留实体关系、以及轨迹训练与贡献分配的核查相关，但属世界模型生成领域，具体可迁移性需核查。
